title: New Bleach Final Season Trailer Reveals First Look at Anime Finale After Hiatus – Watch Now
content:
Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War is soon officially making its return from a month long hiatus for the anime’s final two episodes ever, and now fans have gotten the first look at what to expect from the grand finale with a slick new trailer. Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War – The Calamity hit a surprising snag a month ago when it suddenly announced that the production team would need additional time to work on the final two episodes of the anime. Thankfully, the additional wait will soon be over.

With the final season of the series going on hiatus for the last month to work on the final two episodes, Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War – The Calamity is coming back later this week with the first of these final two episodes . Giving fans the first look at this final battle against Yhwach (which already seems to be expanded from Tite Kubo’s Bleach manga version), you can check out the final trailer for Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War below to get ready.

When Do Bleach ‘s Final Episodes Come Out?

As previously confirmed by Viz Media, Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War – The Calamity Episode 49 will be making its debut with Hulu and Hulu on Disney+ on October 19th at 8:30AMPT, and then it will be followed by Episode 50 releasing on October 26th at 8:30AM PT. This will be the Japanese audio release with English subtitles. I f you are more interested in the English dub release , however, it has also been revealed that the dubbed version of Episode 49 will be debuting on November 23rd at 8:30AM PT followed by Episode 50 on November 30th at 8:30AM PT

Very important new additions to the cast have been revealed ahead of Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War – The Calamity ‘s official finale as well. It has been announced that Kazui Kurosaki will be voiced by Azusa Tachibana, and Ichika Abarai will be voiced by Ayaka Ohashi . They’ll be making their official debuts in the epilogue following the fight with Yhwach, but English dub voice cast for these new additions (or their relative screen time in these final episodes) have yet to be confirmed as of this time. It’s just another reason to be excited for what’s next.

How Is Bleach’ s Anime Going to End?

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War has made plenty of changes to Kubo’s original manga version of the events through all four seasons of its run thus far, and that’s certainly going to be the case with the finale . The original version of this final fight was relatively short as Kubo was seemingly rushed to his conclusion during the manga’s final weeks with Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine, but the anime has extended it with Yhwach fully invading all three territories. There are all sorts of characters now in the mix for this fight as a result.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War – The Calamity is going to end with these final two episodes either way, but there’s still more planned for the franchise. Bleach Fes. has been announced as a special event coming to Japan next February to celebrate the anime’s grand finale, so fans are hoping to see some possible news of an anime continuation to come from it. Either way, it’s been a long road for this series that fans will see come to an end.

What are you hoping to see from Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War ‘s final two episodes? Can you believe it’s really the end? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: We Are Aliens Film Wins Sitges Film Festival's Anima't Award
content:
Other Japanese films which have won the award are Makoto Shinkai 's your name. in 2016 and Mamoru Hosoda 's Mirai in 2018. However, Kadowaki, who just turned 30 on October 14, is the youngest Japanese director to achieve this feat.

We Are Aliens centers on Tsubasa and Gyōtarō, two boys who as elementary school students became close friends, but jealousy and misunderstandings eventually drove them apart. Years have passed and the two boys have gone in different directions in life. But when the memories from their past come back, they must face what happened between them years ago.

The film stars Ryōta Bandō ( Fureru. , live-action How to Train Your Dragon's Japanese dub ) as Tsubasa, and Amane Okayama ( Blue Giant , live-action I''s , Hirayasumi ) as Gyōtarō, when both characters are young adults. Child actors Yūto Maki and Tasuku Nakagome — who were both selected through auditions — voice Tsubasa and Gyōtarō, respectively, when they were younger. Other cast members include Sakurazaka46 idol group member Ten Yamasaki as Konatsu, comedian Kemuri Matsui as Batahara, Gaku Sano as Tsubasa's friend Seiya Toda, Reika Ōzeki as young Seiya, Arisa Sasaki as Toda's friend Elmo Matsushita, and Edo Harumi as a calligraphy teacher.

We Are Aliens opened in Japan on September 15. The film screened at the Directors' Fortnight of the Cannes Film Festival on May 14, and screened in competition at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival, which ran from June 21 to 27. The Melbourne International Film Festival (MIFF), the New Zealand International Film Festival (NZIFF), and the "Japanese Animation Special: Masterpieces of Madness, Exhilarating Prospects 12+1" category of the 31st Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) also screened the film. Ottawa International Animation Festival awarded the film the Grand Prize for Animated Feature last month.

Kadowaki, who created the second BEASTARS season's ending sequence and music videos for YOASOBI , served as the film's planner, scriptwriter, director, storyboard artist, and editor. Yaffle — who previously produced music for Fujii Kaze, Kenshi Yonezu , and others — composed the music. NOTHING NEW planned and produced the film, and French studio Miyu Productions ( Ghost Cat Anzu , A New Dawn ) collaborated on the production, after joining on the project in June 2025. Artist adieu performs the film's theme song "Sasakure" (Split).

title: Aikatsu Stars 10th Anniversary Film's Trailer Unveils Theme Song, January 22 Debut
content:
Bandai Namco Pictures presented the full trailer and a key visual for Aikatsu Stars! Hoshiboshi no Progress (The Progress of the Stars), the film celebrating the 10th anniversary of the Aikatsu Stars! anime, during a fan meeting event for the film on Saturday. The trailer announces the film's January 22 opening, and it also previews the main theme song "Five stars." Sena, Rie, Miki, Nanase, and Kana perform both this song and the ending theme song "Anata e" (To You).

The tagline of the film is, "Our (rainbow-colored) dream isn't over yet."

The film begins just before the graduation of Yume and the others, when they receive an invitation from Neo Venus Ark's Elza to perform in the "Venus Jamboree" event among the world's top idols. A mysterious passenger ship, the Petit Venus Ark , appears before them.

The Aikatsu Stars! anime series director Teruo Sato returns to direct the new film at Bandai Namco Pictures . Original series head writer Yūko Kakihara is also back to write the film's scenario. The original series' character designer Yukiko Aikei performs the same role for the film. Bandai Namco Pictures is distributing the film.

The Aikatsu Stars! television anime series debuted on TV Tokyo and affiliated channels in April 2016, and ended in March 2018 with 100 episodes. The first Aikatsu Stars! anime film opened in August 2016.

Aikatsu Stars! was followed in the franchise by the Aikatsu Friends! anime from April 2018 to September 2019, the Aikatsu on Parade! anime from October 2019 to July 2020, the hybrid anime/live-action series Aikatsu! Planet in January to June 2021, and finally the franchise 's first foray into a YouTube -exclusive VTuber project with Aikatsu! Academy! in July 2024. Aikatsu! Planet also got an anime film in July 2022.

The Aikatsu! franchise began with the original arcade card game in October 2012. The game inspired a television anime that ran from 2012 to 2016, and three anime films. Each of the successive anime installments of the franchise had their own associated arcade card game ( Aikatsu! Academy! , as a YouTube -exclusive project, has no associated anime and arcade card game).

The Aikatsu! 10th Story ~Mirai e no Starway~ (Starway to the Future) anime film is the overall franchise 's 10th anniversary film, and it opened in Japan in January 2023. The brand-new story for the original Aikatsu! series reunites that series' director Ryuichi Kimura , scenario writer Yoichi Kato , and character designer Hiroko Yaguchi . The project is set in the story of the 2012 to 2016 Aikatsu! anime, and centers once again on protagonist Ichigo Hoshinomiya.

title: Stranger Than Heaven Game Streams Story Trailer for 1st Act 'Kokura'
content:
Sega began streaming a story trailer for Ryu ga Gotoku Studio's Stranger Than Heaven game (previously codenamed "Project Century") on Friday. The video outlines the game's first act "Kokura," and "depicts the events that led Daito, who had endured persecution in America, to stow away on the 'ghost ship' of the merchant Orpheus in pursuit of Japan."

The game will explore different times and places in Japan's modern history, including Kokura, Fukuoka in 1915; Kure, Hiroshima in 1929; Minami, Osaka in 1943; Atami, Shizuoka in 1951; and the fictional neighborhood of Kamurocho (based on the Kabukicho neighborhood, and a constant setting of RGG Studio's Yakuza/Like a Dragon games) in Shinjuku, Tokyo in 1965.

Sega describes the game's story:

A 50-year saga of those with nowhere to go and their desperate struggle to find a home. In 1915 San Francisco, a young boy, Makoto Daito, sneaks aboard a suspicious ship in the harbor under the cover of night. Born to an American father and a Japanese mother, Makoto faces harsh persecution due to his Asian heritage. After losing both of his parents, Makoto decides to travel to his mother's homeland, Japan, where a fateful encounter awaits. With nothing but the shirt on his back, Makoto soon learns, however, that his voyage across the Pacific is anything but a "free ride," and that this one choice will forever change the course of his life.

The cast includes:

• Yū Shirota as Makoto Daito

• Snoop Dogg as Orpheus

• Moeka Hoshi as Tae Matsumoto

• Tori Kelly as Suzy Day

• Akio Ōtsuka as Heigo Yashima

• Tokuma Nishioka as Kiyoshi Otsuru

• Satoshi Fujihara as Takashi

• Cordell Broadus as The Veiled Stranger

• Ado as Keiko Shirai

• Bunta Sugawara (model basis) and Takashi Ukaji (voice) as Genzo Iwaki

• Late American rapper Tupac

• Takaya Kuroda (who plays Kazuma Kiryu in Ryu ga Gotoku's related Yakuza/Like a Dragon series)

• Kouhei Tsuji

• Yasukaze Motomiya (who plays Kosei Shishido in the Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name game and Kazuma Kiryu in Nihon Tohitsu's live-action Like a Dragon Powered By Nihon Touitsu series)

Sega provided the following comment regarding the character Genzo Iwaki and the model for the character being based on the late actor Bunta Sugawara :

In STRANGER THAN HEAVEN , the late and legendary actor Bunta Sugawara appears. SEGA received formal consent from his family, and, with materials provided by Toei Company Ltd. —which produced many of Mr. Sugawara's films, including the Battles Without Honor and Humanity — RGG Studio crafted his CG character design based on archival footage and photographs from the time.

Snoop Dogg , Satoshi Fujihara , Ado, and Tori Kelly perform the game's theme song "Stranger Than Heaven." The song will get a release this year.

The game is inspiring a live-action film on Netflix .

Yakuza Kiwami 3 & Dark Ties , Ryu ga Gotoku Studio's remake of the Yakuza 3 game along with the new standalone Dark Ties title, launched as a single release for PlayStation 5, PlayStation 4, Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Steam worldwide on February 12.

title: Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War - The Calamity Anime Streams 'Last' Promo Video
content:
The official YouTube channel for the Bleach franchise began streaming on Friday "the last" promotional video for Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War - The Calamity , the fourth and final part of the Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War anime.

The Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War anime has been running for four cours (quarter of a year) with breaks in between.

The anime covers the rest of the original manga up through its ending. The Thousand Year Blood War arc is the final arc of the manga, and covers volumes 55-74.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War - The Calamity debuted on July 25 on the TV Tokyo channel at 11:00 p.m. JST (10:00 a.m. EDT). The anime began streaming on Japanese streaming services on July 26 at noon.

jo0ji performs the opening theme song "I-BULL" and singer-songwriter 9Lana performs the ending theme song "Rasen" (Spiral).

Viz Media and Fathom Entertainment screened in advance Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War - The Calamity 's first three episodes in U.S. theaters on June 25-29.
author: ANN

The titles include (some titles do not yet have release dates):

title: Comikey Adds Mato Kauta's The Wolf King's Bride Manga
content:
Comikey announced on Friday it has licensed Mato Kauta 's The Wolf King’s Bride ( Ōkami-Heika no Hanayome ) manga. The company released the first five chapters digitally, and will add new chapters every Friday.

Comikey describes the story:

"If you leak this matter out to anyone, even by accident..." Yurin, the daughter of a low-level official, came into the royal palace after hearing about an amazing job with high pay. Unfortunately for her, that work entailed playing the role of a bride for the cold and ruthless Wolf King, Haku Reisho. After starting her work within the rear palace that's rife with conspiracy, Yurin learned of His Majesty's secret. What will become of her fate?!

Comikey had announced in August it will release several shōjo manga titles from Hakusensha 's catalogue in English digitally, and teased an image that had featured the manga.

Kauta serialized the manga in Hakusensha 's LaLa magazine from 2009 to 2018, and the manga has 19 volumes. The manga has not previously had an English release.

Other new manga Comikey has released or will release in October includes:

• Soukai Studio's How I Became the Duke's Beloved Daughter webtoon (October 7)

• Nozomu Amaike and Kenichi Kisaragi's Local Farmer Kills Dragon, Outs Himself as The Strongest in the Land! manga (October 12)

• Kizu Kanoda, Yukiko Tadano, and Shisseki's At Home with a Girl in Her Cute Pajamas manga (October 14)

• Tomoki Matsumoto and LOSA's The Bound Hero Knows No Fear manga (October 19)

• Inariyama's My Faceless Classmate, Wakao manga (October 21)

• Punichan and Maro Yanagiya's I'm the Demon Lord, but For Some Reason the Hero's Infatuated With Me manga (October 26)

contentBlocks.text: Comikey announced on Friday it has licensed Mato Kauta 's The Wolf King’s Bride ( Ōkami-Heika no Hanayome ) manga. The company released the first five chapters digitally, and will add new chapters every Friday.
Comikey describes the story:

"If you leak this matter out to anyone, even by accident..." Yurin, the daughter of a low-level official, came into the royal palace after hearing about an amazing job with high pay. Unfortunately for her, that work entailed playing the role of a bride for the cold and ruthless Wolf King, Haku Reisho. After starting her work within the rear palace that's rife with conspiracy, Yurin learned of His Majesty's secret. What will become of her fate?!
Comikey had announced in August it will release several shōjo manga titles from Hakusensha 's catalogue in English digitally, and teased an image that had featured the manga.
Kauta serialized the manga in Hakusensha 's LaLa magazine from 2009 to 2018, and the manga has 19 volumes. The manga has not previously had an English release.
Other new manga Comikey has released or will release in October includes:
Soukai Studio's How I Became the Duke's Beloved Daughter webtoon (October 7)
Nozomu Amaike and Kenichi Kisaragi's Local Farmer Kills Dragon, Outs Himself as The Strongest in the Land! manga (October 12)

Tomoki Matsumoto and LOSA's The Bound Hero Knows No Fear manga (October 19)
Inariyama's My Faceless Classmate, Wakao manga (October 21)

taskey's The Black-Winged Emperor Adores the Shunned Saint in the Tower webtoon (October 28)
Bodax, Kaoruho Hananami, and Jio Miyata's I'm Marrying the Pauper Count of a Remote Frontier, So I'll Work Hard to Reform his Territory ～The Letter From Boule～ manga (October 30)

title: Peow2 Licenses Jyoshikohei, Alien 9, Phantom Core Manga
content:
Sweden-based comic publisher Peow2 announced on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday it has licensed three new manga for English release: Jiro Matsumoto 's Jyoshikohei , Hitoshi Tomizawa 's Alien 9 , and Yasushi Nirasawa 's Phantom Core .

‼️INCOMING LICENSE💥 Jyoshikohei by Jiro Matsumoto . Giant high school girl mechs rule the dimensional battlefield, but they drive their middle-aged male pilots insane. Takigawa's job? Brutally hunt down the ones that go rogue. Coming 2027, 3 new omnibus editions from Peow2 [image or embed] — Peow2 ( @peow.bsky.social ) October 14, 2026 at 1:53 AM

Matsumoto launched Jyoshikohei in 2011. Shinchosha published the seventh and final volume in December 2015. Peow2 describes the story:

Giant high school girl mechs rule the dimensional battlefield, but they drive their middle-aged male pilots insane. Takigawa's job? Brutally hunt down the ones that go rogue.

The company will release the manga in an omnibus format in three volumes starting in 2027. The first volume will feature an A3-size poster with new artwork from Matsumoto.

Vertical published Matsumoto's Velveteen & Mandala manga in English, and Kodama Tales has licensed Matsumoto's beautiful place manga.

🪲INCOMING LICENSE‼️ Alien 9 -The Complete- by Hitoshi Tomizawa Grimcute sci-fi?! A grade school Alien Defense Force risks their lives on a daily basis to dispatch aliens that are constantly trying to invade their school. It's sticky, slimy, scary work, but somebody has gotta do it. Coming 2027 [image or embed] — Peow2 ( @peow.bsky.social ) October 15, 2026 at 12:35 AM

Peow2 will release the Alien 9 manga in 2027, and it describes the story:

Grimcute sci-fi?! A grade school Alien Defense Force risks their lives on a daily basis to dispatch aliens that are constantly trying to invade their school. It's sticky, slimy, scary work, but somebody has gotta do it.

Central Park Media previously released part of the manga in English in 2003. The manga ran from 1998 to 1999 and Akita Shoten published three volumes.

The manga inspired a four-episode OVA that debuted in May 2001. Central Park Media previously released the series in North America, and AnimEigo re-released the series on Blu-ray Disc on June 9.

Peow2 will release Phantom Core in spring 2027 and it describes the story:

Monster lovers rejoice!!! The companion sci-fi/fantasy manga to our upcoming release CREATURE CORE. Follow Phancure, the beer loving freelance suppressor and Nina Dolono hunt down demented WEPTURES!

Hobby Japan originally serialized the manga in Hobby Japan Extra magazine

Peow2 is also releasing Nirasawa's Creature Core collection of works and artbook in English.

Nirasawa is known for his design and modeling work on television series and films such as Garo , Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within , and several Heisei-era Kamen Rider series.

Nirasawa died in 2016 at the age of 52 from kidney failure.
